Sunlight takes about 8 minutes 20 seconds to reach Earth, and about 43 minutes to reach Jupiter on average. Light travels 299,792 km every second, so what we see in the sky is always light that left earlier.

review.notes: Semantic review: every number traces to a sourced fact (NIST speed of light; NASA Sun and Jupiter facts). Averages are stated as averages ('about', 'on average'); the Sun's light time is the average 1 AU figure, not the December value (about 8 min 10 s). The Jupiter sentence was corrected to say sunlight takes 43 minutes to reach Jupiter, not that the light we see left it that long ago (reflected light travels back separately). No time of day, direction or position claim.
